summary.text: Hemoglobin is an iron-containing protein in red blood cells that helps transport oxygen.
In the blood it carries oxygen from the lungs or gills to the other tissues of the body, where it releases it for aerobic respiration.
It also carries some of the body’s carbon dioxide and the regulatory molecule nitric oxide.

facts.label: Subunits
facts.value: Four in the most common mammalian type

facts.label: Oxygen per molecule
facts.value: Up to four oxygen molecules in mammals

items.prompt: Hemoglobin lets blood carry far more oxygen than gas dissolved in plasma alone. By roughly how much?

options.label: About twofold
About seventy-fold
About tenfold
About a thousandfold

items.explain: Its oxygen-binding capacity increases total blood oxygen capacity seventy-fold compared with dissolved oxygen alone.

items.prompt: Leghemoglobin is a hemoglobin variant in the nitrogen-fixing nodules of leguminous plants. What does it do there?

options.label: Scavenges oxygen away so it cannot poison the nodules
Delivers extra oxygen to the nodules
Carries carbon dioxide out of the roots
Stores the nitrogen the nodules fix

items.explain: It scavenges oxygen away from anaerobic systems such as nitrogen-fixing nodules, preventing oxygen poisoning.

items.prompt: As two species get more distantly related, how do their hemoglobin sequences usually change?

options.label: They stay exactly identical
The differences shrink
Only the iron count changes
The differences grow larger

items.explain: Globin sequences usually differ between species, with the difference growing with evolutionary distance.

items.prompt: Sickle-cell disease is one of a group of hereditary diseases caused by hemoglobin gene mutations. What is the group called?

options.label: Thalassemias
Hemoglobinemias
Hemoglobinopathies
Carbaminohemoglobins

items.explain: Mutations in hemoglobin genes can cause hemoglobinopathies, of which sickle-cell disease is the best known.

items.prompt: Hemoglobin's name joins two words, one for each part of a subunit's makeup. What do they refer to?

options.label: An embedded iron-holding group and a globular protein
A red blood pigment and a blood plasma protein
A gas-carrying ring and a segment of a gene
A single iron ion and a cell membrane pump

items.explain: The name comes from heme and globin: each subunit is a globular protein with an embedded heme group holding an iron atom.

items.prompt: A person has too much sugar in their blood. What can happen to their hemoglobin?

options.label: It can lose all of its iron atoms
Glucose can attach to it and raise its A1c level
It can split into four separate chains
It can stop binding any oxygen at all

items.explain: Excessive glucose in the blood can attach to hemoglobin and raise the level of hemoglobin A1c.
